details:
What it does
FieldRewind is a web app that helps farmers explore crop-rotation options that could improve soil health and make their farm more resilient to changing weather and water conditions. Our demo uses a real corn–soybean field in central Iowa.

The farmer starts by viewing their field on a satellite map, along with its real soil profile and crop history. They set their priorities: saving water, protecting soil, cutting input costs, or earning extra income. Then they press play on Rewind, a time-lapse of roughly 10 years of satellite greenness (NDVI) for their exact field. It shows when the soil sits bare and which seasons were stressful. A weak-spot calendar then shows which months the field is most exposed to heavy rain, heat stress, frost and dry spells.

Next, FieldRewind compares three rotation strategies: the farmer’s current corn–soybean rotation, the same rotation with a cereal rye winter cover crop, and an extended three-year rotation with oats and red clover. Each is scored on water use, erosion protection, soil organic matter, nitrogen supply, pest-cycle disruption and income stability. The rankings update live as the farmer changes their priorities. For every strategy, the app explains why it was suggested, what evidence supports it, its benefits, where information is missing, and what a local expert should check. What-if sliders let farmers test hotter, drier or stormier futures and watch the rankings change. A Demo mode plays the whole story in about 90 seconds, and a printable Field report summarises everything to take to an agronomist.

How it works
A data pipeline downloads real data for the field: daily temperature, rainfall and soil wetness from NASA POWER; NDVI from MODIS (MOD13Q1); crop history from the USDA Cropland Data Layer; and soil properties from USDA SSURGO. A transparent rule-based model turns these into scores grounded in published agronomy, including Iowa State University’s long-term Marsden Farm rotation study. Every score shows its reasoning, the data behind it and a confidence level. It is intentionally not a black box.

Benefits and impact
Farmers rarely get to see their own field’s history from space, or compare rotation options side by side using their own priorities. FieldRewind turns complex satellite data into a simple story: when your field is vulnerable, and what could protect it. It is a support tool, not a decision-maker. It never says “plant this”, and it points farmers to local experts to verify any option.

Tools used
TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Recharts and MapLibre GL, deployed on Netlify. The app was built with AI assistance (Claude Code). No hardware was needed.

What makes it creative
Instead of another dashboard of charts, FieldRewind treats satellite data as a story the farmer can watch and play with: rewind the past, spot the weak points, then test the future.

Factors we considered
Farmers with little technical experience (plain language, glossary tooltips, few numbers at once), honesty about uncertainty (confidence levels, labelled estimates), the difference between satellite and ground measurements, farmer-specific constraints like equipment and livestock, and keeping farmer judgment and local expertise at the centre.
